parsed.n_justification: The domain spans 900-3300 m and the brief flags elevation as a key candidate driver of rain/snow partitioning and ET. Three columns (low desert-scrub, mid-elevation woodland, high-elevation conifer/snow zone) resolve the dominant elevation gradient while keeping the site-archetype design tractable; each is run for both 1993 and 2002 to isolate the wet/dry-year contrast.
requires_capabilities: single-column ELM (I-compset, satellite phenology or BGC)
accelerated-decomposition + final spinup prior to transient run
surface dataset with site-specific soil texture and PFT
assumptions: Run is initialized 1991-01-01 following AD/final spinup and integrated 12 years to fully cover both the 1993 wet year and 2002 dry year with consistent antecedent conditions.

Wet/dry-year designation (1993 wet, 2002 dry) reflects regional precipitation anomalies; each elevation column experiences the same forcing years so partitioning differences are driven by climate and elevation-dependent phase (rain vs. snow).
Single-column QRUNOFF represents locally generated runoff, not gauge streamflow; comparisons to USGS are qualitative (relative wet/dry response).
Default satellite-phenology vegetation appropriate to each elevation band (desert shrub, evergreen/deciduous woodland, needleleaf evergreen forest) is used.
Monthly and daily history output enabled to compute annual water-budget closure and seasonal snowmelt-driven partitioning.
